354755.title: NP-completeness of the planar graph square-root problem
354755.literal_statement:
A graph $G$ is **planar** if it can be drawn in the plane without edge crossings. For a graph class $\mathcal{H}$, the $\mathcal{H}$-square-root problem asks whether a given graph has a square root belonging to $\mathcal{H}$.

**Planar square-root conjecture.** The $\mathcal{H}$-square-root problem is NP-complete for the class $\mathcal{H}$ of planar graphs.

The paper proves NP-completeness for the class of $6$-apex graphs, which is minor-closed and lies at the bottom of the bounded-expansion hierarchy. It remains open whether the apex vertices are necessary, or whether the planar square-root problem is already hard.
354755.ordinary_derivation_failure_or_unpaid_le: Planar root NP-hardness needs an exact reduction with a planar root in every YES case and no extraneous roots in NO cases. Source Theorems1.1–1.2 allow six apex vertices. Removing them loses the global constraint mechanism; no planar replacement is proved. NP membership alone is not resolution.

354861.title: The classification conjecture for Laplacian-realizable sets $S_{\{i,n\}_n^m}$
354861.literal_statement: For integers $n$, $m$, and $i$ with $1\leqslant i<n$, let $S_{\{i,n\}_n^m}$ denote the multiset obtained from $\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ by deleting $i$ and $n$, and repeating $m$ once, with $m\ne0$ so that the corresponding graph is connected. A set is **Laplacian realizable** if it is the Laplacian spectrum of a connected simple graph on $n$ vertices. **The classification conjecture.** For $n\geqslant4$, the only Laplacian-realizable sets of kind $S_{\{i,n\}_n^m}$ are $S_{\{4,6\}_6^3}$, $S_{\{2,6\}_6^3}$, $S_{\{7,8\}_8^3}$, and $S_{\{1,8\}_8^5}$. The conjecture is motivated by the complete search through order $8$ described in the paper and by the structural results on Cartesian products; no resolution beyond those cases is supplied.

355014.title: Hanging-elements conjecture for the combinatorial derived matroid
355014.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid with set of circuits $\mathcal{C}$. For $S\subseteq\mathcal{C}$, let $\operatorname{supp}(S)$ be the union of the circuits in $S$, and let $\mathcal{A}$ be the collection of dependent sets defining the combinatorial derived matroid $\delta M$. **Hanging-elements conjecture.** If $S\notin\mathcal{A}$ and $C\in\mathcal{C}$ has an element outside $\operatorname{supp}(S)$, then

$$
S\cup\{C\}\notin\mathcal{A}.
$$

The statement is proposed as an analogue of a known result for the Oxley–Wang derived matroid, but the paper explains that the analogous claim for $\mathcal{A}_0$ is insufficient and that new ideas are needed.

355138.literal_statement:

**Deletion conjecture.** Every $(k,\ell)$-crucial permutation can be obtained by deleting elements from a maximal $(k,\ell)$-crucial permutation.

355297.title: The convex-radii cover conjecture for metric trees
355297.literal_statement:
Let $(r_1,\dots,r_k)$ be a sequence of non-negative real numbers satisfying

$$
r_1\leq r_2-r_1\leq r_3-r_2\leq\cdots\leq r_k-r_{k-1},
$$

so that $(r_1,\dots,r_k)$ is **convex**. Let $T$ be a metric tree with total length $|T|\leq 2\sum_{i=1}^k r_i$. **Convex-radii cover conjecture.** The sequence $(r_1,\dots,r_k)$ is a cover of $T$.
This conjecture is a metric analogue of the Burning Number Conjecture and includes the sequence $(1,\ldots,k)$. The source presents it as a broad natural class for which the covering property should hold; its general status is not resolved there.

355475.title: Signed quadratic quotient-product congruence
355475.literal_statement:
Let $S_{(p-1)/2}$ be the symmetric group on $1,\ldots,(p-1)/2$, and let $\operatorname{sign}(\tau)$ denote permutation sign. **Signed quadratic quotient-product conjecture.** Let $p>3$ be a prime with $p\equiv3\pmod4$. Then

$$
\sum_{\tau\in S_{(p-1)/2}}\operatorname{sign}(\tau)\prod_{\substack{j=1\\\\ \tau(j)\ne j}}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{j^2+\tau(j)^2}{j^2-\tau(j)^2}\equiv0\pmod{p^2}.
$$

When $p\equiv7\pmod8$,

$$
\sum_{\tau\in S_{(p-1)/2}}\operatorname{sign}(\tau)\prod_{\substack{j=1\\\\ \tau(j)\ne j}}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{j^2+\tau(j)^2}{j^2-\tau(j)^2}\equiv0\pmod{p^3}.
$$

The second congruence strengthens the first for primes in the indicated residue class; the supplied text gives no resolution.

Complete determinant expansion/denominator and residue bridge in ORDINARY; proof passages read. Auxiliary coefficient identities not independently audited. 355550.title: Top-degree HOMFLY conjecture for arbitrary plabic graphs
355550.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a plabic graph with $\operatorname{c}(G)$ connected components and $n$ interior faces. Let $L^{\operatorname{plab}}_G$ be its associated plabic graph link, and let $\Ptop_L(q)$ be obtained from the top $a$-degree term of its HOMFLY polynomial by the stated specialization. **Top-degree HOMFLY conjecture.**

$$
\deg_a^{\operatorname{top}}P(L^{\operatorname{plab}}_G)=\operatorname{c}(G)-n-1,
$$

$$
\deg(\Ptop_L(q))=n,
$$

and the leading coefficient of $\Ptop_L(q)$ is $1$. This is presented as a basic extension beyond simple plabic graphs, including graphs with interior leaves. The supplied source gives no resolution status.

355551.title: Full HOMFLY invariance under mutation for connected simple plabic graphs
355551.literal_statement:
Let $G$ and $G'$ be connected simple plabic graphs whose quivers $Q_G$ and $Q_{G'}$ are mutation equivalent. Let $L^{\operatorname{plab}}_G$ and $L^{\operatorname{plab}}_{G'}$ be their associated plabic graph links. **Full HOMFLY invariance conjecture.**

$$
P(L^{\operatorname{plab}}_G;a,z)=P(L^{\operatorname{plab}}_{G'};a,z).
$$

This asserts that the full HOMFLY polynomial, unlike the link itself in general, is determined by the mutation class of the quiver for connected simple plabic graphs. The supplied source gives no resolution status.
